scenario.title: Approval and decision types
situations: The user asks to approve a change before it finishes.
A QA reviewer cannot determine the result from captured evidence.
A release reaches a configured sign-off stage.
A team wants any one approver or every named approver to decide.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Inspected policy/docs and lifecycle review code; no live approval, authority check or Inbox card was exercised.
Harness tool permission and machine-connection approval are separate security/access concepts owned by other map families.
Command nodes, when present, were checked with installed CLI --help only; this proves parser/help availability, not serving-control-plane capability or successful execution.

lessons.title: Identify what this yes changes
lessons.when: When the first work-approval, evidence-review or release-approval request appears.
lessons.need: Work approval, QA evidence review and release approval settle different obligations. Each card should name its subject, evidence, decision and consequence. A delivery notice asks for nothing.
lessons.surface: Inbox, item QA and run pages; workflow approval defaults
lessons.gap: Current cards carry these distinctions; catalog has no explicit approval-learning situation. Review question: should JOURNEYS add a first-decision explanation that links its exact evidence?

lessons.title: Persist the approval the user actually requested
lessons.when: At intake when the user asks for screenshots, visual proof, conditional review or explicit personal approval.
lessons.need: A screenshot alone does not add approval. Unconditional human review differs from human-if-unsure; use the correct item-scoped policy and named reviewer, without modifying shared defaults for one request.
lessons.surface: Idea/Dash delivery evidence intake; QA verdict-mode contract
lessons.gap: Review question: should FIRST-USER D include explicit approve-it versus show-evidence scenarios so successful QA cannot silently skip requested review?

lessons.title: Apply the actual decision policy
lessons.when: Before presenting or recording a decision, especially when multiple people or roles must approve.
lessons.need: Any-one and all-required policies differ. An agent must inspect the typed request and current policy; one generic approve command cannot settle all decision kinds.
lessons.surface: Workflow approval explanation; lifecycle gate; run-only Approve skill
lessons.gap: Review question: should Help route approve this from the actual pending request instead of leaving the user to guess the command?
